title: Psalm emits this issue when there a property defined on an enum, as PHP does not allow user-defined properties on enums.
summary: Psalm reports it at each error level.

title: Psalm emits this issue when trying to fetch a property on an interface as interfaces, by definition, do not have definitions for properties.
summary: Psalm ignores it at error level 5 and higher.

title: Psalm emits this issue when Psalm invalidated all possible types for a given expression.
summary: It is often an indication that Psalm found dead code or that documented types were not exhaustive. Psalm reports it at each error level.

title: Psalm emits this issue when a public or protected class property has a different docblock type to the matching property in the parent class.
summary: Psalm ignores it at error level 4 and higher.

title: Psalm emits this issue when a public or protected class property has a different type to the matching property in the parent class.
summary: Psalm reports it at each error level.

title: Psalm emits this issue when calling a non-static function statically.
summary: Psalm reports it at each error level.

title: Psalm emits this issue when a function returns by reference expression that is not a variable.
summary: Psalm ignores it at error level 8.
